requirement.evidence: It is unlawful for a landlord to use an algorithmic device to set rental rates or occupancy levels for residential rental property.
requirement.note: Also supported: sale/license ban in 98.1103(a) and tenant remedies in 98.1104(a) (injunctive relief, damages, civil penalties up to $1,000 per violation, attorney's fees).

key_value.evidence: For each month a violation of section 98.1103(b) exists or continues, and for each residential rental property a landlord uses an algorithmic device, it shall constitute a separate and distinct violation.
key_value.note: The $1,000 cap is in 98.1104(a): "A tenant may seek injunctive relief, damages, or civil penalties of up to $1,000 per violation of this Division, in a civil action against a landlord." The separate-violation rule applies to 98.1103(b) use violations.

status.evidence: Councilmember Sean Elo-Rivera proposes to protect San Diegans from automated rent price-fixing by banning the sale, license, and use of automated rent-setting software that advises or recommends rental rates or occupancy levels.
status.note: Document shows an unadopted draft: ordinance number and date of final passage are blank, and the council adoption certification is unsigned. Pending as of 2026-10-01 is consistent with the document, though it does not show later action.

citation.evidence: Amend San Diego Municipal Code Chapter 9, Article 8 by adding new Division 11, sections 98.1101, 98.1102, 98.1103, and 98.1104, to adopt the proposed Prohibition of Anti-Competitive Automated Rent Price-Fixing Ordinance.
